results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Apex Devastator, Call Forth the Tempest and Creative Technique.
results.text:
I call this deck **Red Tempest Technique**. It's a brew, accepted as legal.

**Plan:** Use Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors, Chrome Mox, Simian Spirit Guide and Lotus Petal to cast Creative Technique (5 mana) on turn 2 or 3. Technique casts a random nonland card from the deck for free. The deck is built so that card is usually a payoff, and the best one is Apex Devastator. When Apex is cast this way, all four of its cascades trigger. They often find Call Forth the Tempest, which cascades twice more and then damages each enemy creature for the total mana value of everything else you cast that turn (Apex alone adds 10). That clears their board, and the 10/10 Apex plus the cascaded threats finish the game around turn 4.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Sneak and Show style:** Show and Tell into Omniscience, then cast Apex for free. It works, but it's a worse Sneak and Show and Creative Technique barely has a job there.
2. **Green-red ramp with rituals and Elvish Spirit Guide:** Every ritual is also a card Creative Technique can flip, and those are wasted flips.
3. **Mono-Red Prison's fast mana and free spells (chosen):** No published list runs your three cards together, so I took this package from the menu. Its fast mana is mostly lands, so it doesn't fill the deck with cards Technique can flip and waste. Its free spells (Fury, Pyrokinesis) are good flips. I dropped Chalice of the Void because a free Chalice is a wasted flip, and Blood Moon/Magus because they would turn our own Tomb and City into Mountains.

**How the pieces fit:**
- **Good free hits:** 24 of the 44 nonland cards are strong when cast free: Apex, Call Forth, Fury, Pyrokinesis, The One Ring and Fable. A second Technique also counts, since it just rolls again.
- **Stuck in hand:**
  - Call Forth and Technique copies stuck in hand can be exiled to pay for Fury and Pyrokinesis (both cost "exile a red card").
  - A stuck Apex can go under Chrome Mox.
- **Hard-casting:** Tomb and City make hard-casting the 8-mana Call Forth possible later in the game.

**Honest odds and weak spots:**
- **Speed:** You'll see at least one Creative Technique by turn 3 on the play only about 49% of the time. The rest of the deck has to buy time: free removal, Fable, The One Ring, and Broadside Bombardiers for pressure.
- **Simulator number:** The checker gives 2% for drawing every card in the win line by turn 4. That's misleading here, because Apex and Call Forth are meant to come from the library through Technique and cascade, not from your hand. Still, the full line is a good draw, not a sure thing.
- **Demonstrate:** Creative Technique lets you copy it, but then the opponent gets a copy too. Only use it when you're ahead.
- **Lands:** The deck runs 16 lands, below the checker's general suggestion of about 20. That matches real Mono-Red Prison lists (about 16.8) built on the same fast mana.

**Sideboard:** Leyline of the Void and Faerie Macabre against graveyard decks, Pyroblast against the blue tempo decks (Esper, Izzet, Dimir), Fiery Confluence, Disruptor Flute, and Chalice of the Void against Oops All Spells, Doomsday and Lotus Petal combo.

--- After playtest ---
I resubmitted the deck with three changes. One honest number first: drawing Technique and an Ancient Tomb or City of Traitors together by turn 3 happens in only about 35% of games (49% for Technique alone). This is still an all-in brew.

**1. Apex and Call Forth stuck in hand: partly fixed.**
- I cut 1 Call Forth the Tempest and 2 The One Ring, and added 3 Seasoned Pyromancer. Pyromancer discards stuck Apex or Call Forth, draws 2 and makes tokens. It's also red, so it can be pitched to Fury.
- I kept all 4 Apex Devastator. It's the best card Technique can flip and the whole point of your request, and a drawn copy isn't fully dead: it can be exiled to Chrome Mox. Its green mana still pays the generic part of Technique.

**2. Technique flipping mana cards: fixed as suggested.**
- I cut 4 Lotus Petal and 2 Simian Spirit Guide, and added 4 Mountain and 2 Gemstone Caverns.
- That's 6 fewer cards Technique can whiff on. Gemstone Caverns also lets you exile a dead Apex from your opening hand when you're on the draw.
- Turn-2 Technique now needs Tomb + Mountain + Chrome Mox + Spirit Guide. The normal plan is turn 3: Mountain + Tomb + City for 5 mana.

**3. Self-damage: fixed a different way.**
- Cutting 2 Rings cuts the burden damage. The cheap threat the review asked for is Seasoned Pyromancer rather than Laelia, because it also solves problem 1.
- I kept 4 Ancient Tomb. Swapping one for a City of Traitors would hurt the turn-2 and turn-3 Technique starts more than 1–2 life per game would help.

**About the submission check:** it said every card in the win line is drawn by turn 3 in only 0.1% of games. That number is misleading here. Apex, Call Forth and Fury are meant to come from Technique and cascades, not from your hand, and the check doesn't count that.

The sideboard is unchanged.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State.
results.text:
This is a Grixis Phoenix brew that can win fast. Buried Alive puts three Arclight Phoenixes from your library into the graveyard. Phoenix returns at the beginning of combat if you've cast three or more instants and sorceries that turn, so Buried Alive needs two other spells with it. Dark Ritual and Lotus Petal pay for Buried Alive early, and Gut Shot can be the free third spell (you pay 2 life instead of mana).

**The main line:** Land, Dark Ritual (first spell, makes three black mana), Buried Alive (second spell), Gut Shot for 2 life (third spell). Three hasty 3/2 fliers come back and hit for 9. They stay on the battlefield and hit for 9 again next turn, and Lightning Bolt or Gut Shot covers the last few points of damage.

**Flow State's job:** After that turn, the graveyard already holds an instant and a sorcery. That means Flow State puts two of the top three cards into your hand, not one, so you have cards left after spending your hand. Before then, it's just a cheap way to dig for Buried Alive or mana.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Ritual-combo, built on the Doomsday shell (chosen).** It borrows Doomsday's Dark Ritual, Lotus Petal, Brainstorm, Ponder, Force of Will and Thoughtseize, plus its dual-land and fetchland mana. Buried Alive goes in where Doomsday would have Doomsday.
2. **Izzet Tempo with a black splash.** Daze, Bolt and cantrips, with Buried Alive as a late-game value card. It's slower and doesn't use Buried Alive well.
3. **A Reanimator hybrid.** Buried Alive would also find Griselbrand. That spreads the deck across two plans.

I chose the first because Dark Ritual alone lets you cast Buried Alive on turn 1 with a free spell left over. That makes the three cards you asked for a real kill on turns 1–3, not just cards that share a graveyard theme.

**Notes:**
- **Two bans:** Entomb and Gitaxian Probe are banned in Legacy, which is why Gut Shot is the free spell. It sees almost no Legacy play, so the checker flagged it. I kept it because the main line needs a third spell that costs no mana.
- **Odds:** A natural Buried Alive by turn 2 shows up 44.5% of the time. That rises to 93% if you count Buried Alive plus the cantrips that can find it. Having every exact card in the line drawn by turn 3 is rare (the checker says about 1%), but most cards in the line have stand-ins. Lotus Petal can replace Dark Ritual. Brainstorm, Ponder, Bolt or Manamorphose can each be one of the three spells. Faithless Looting or Brainstorm can also get Phoenixes into the graveyard.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - Graveyard hate like Surgical Extraction, which over a quarter of recent lists run, can stop the plan.
  - Orcish Bowmasters' 1-damage ping won't kill a 3/2 Phoenix, but Fatal Push will.
  - The 3 Force of Will and 2 Thoughtseize are there to protect the key turn.
- **Sideboard:**
  - Pyroblast for blue tempo decks.
  - Blood Moon for Tron and Lands.
  - Toxic Deluge for Ocelot Aggro.
  - Surgical Extraction for Reanimator and Oops All Spells.

The deck passed the legality check with no errors.

--- After playtest ---
I resubmitted the deck and it was accepted. I swapped out 4 Gut Shot and 1 Flow State for 2 Faithless Looting, 1 Force of Will and 2 Thoughtseize. The main plan is unchanged: Dark Ritual into Buried Alive, then one more cheap spell, brings back three hasty Phoenixes on turn 1 or 2.

1. **Drawn Phoenixes had no way into the graveyard: fixed.** I cut 2 Gut Shot and added 2 Faithless Looting, so there are now 3. That gives 7 ways to put Phoenix in the graveyard: 4 Buried Alive and 3 Looting. Looting costs one red, so it also counts as one of the three spells, and it can be flashed back for {2}{R} on a later turn.
2. **Flow State was too slow: partly fixed.** I went from 4 to 3, not the suggested 2, because Flow State is one of the cards you asked for. It costs 2 and only gives you two cards once an instant and a sorcery are already in your graveyard. Brainstorm, Ponder, Ritual, Bolt, Looting and Thoughtseize get it there, so it works best after the first turn. The freed slot went to a Thoughtseize. A 5th Lotus Petal isn't possible because the deck already runs the maximum 4.
3. **Buried Alive had too little protection: fixed.** I cut the last 2 Gut Shot and added a 4th Force of Will and a 3rd Thoughtseize. With the Thoughtseize from fix 2, the deck now has 4 Force and 4 Thoughtseize, which is 8 cards to protect the Buried Alive turn. Thoughtseize is also a one-mana sorcery that counts toward the three spells.

Losing Gut Shot means the third spell now costs mana. A second land or a Lotus Petal pays for Lightning Bolt or Faithless Looting after Dark Ritual into Buried Alive.

**Graveyard hate:** The sideboard covers this. Pyroblast goes up to 4 and Fatal Push to 3, replacing the spare Thoughtseize and Force of Will that moved into the main deck. Against Surgical Extraction, the backup plan is hardcasting Phoenix for 4 and getting it back later with Looting.

**Draw odds:** The checker says you'll have every card in the win line by turn 2 in about 0% of games. That number is misleading: it counts every card I listed, including the Phoenixes, which you never need to draw because Buried Alive fetches them. The real requirement is just Dark Ritual, Buried Alive, one more cheap spell, and two lands or a land plus Lotus Petal.

results.prompt: Brew me a Vintage deck built around Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam.
results.text:
I built a red-blue Goblin Welder combo deck (a brew). The shell comes from Legacy's "Sewer Combo", the only real decks that run all three of your cards together, and I added Vintage's fast mana and blue power cards.

**How it wins:** Get Goblin Welder on the battlefield with Sewer-veillance Cam in play and Legion Extruder in your graveyard (or the reverse). Tap Welder to sacrifice Cam and bring back Extruder:
- Extruder enters and deals 2 damage.
- Cam leaving the battlefield untaps Welder.
- Tap Welder again to swap Extruder for Cam. Cam entering untaps Welder again.

The loop costs no mana, so it deals as much damage as you want, to the opponent or to their creatures. You only need three cards. Goblin Engineer's enter trigger puts Extruder or Cam straight into the graveyard. Melded Moxite, Wheel of Fortune, Gamble and Thundering Falls also get pieces into the graveyard. Skateboard gives a Welder haste so it can start the loop the turn it lands, and Agatha's Soul Cauldron can give Welder's ability to another creature if Welder dies.

**Directions I considered:**
1. A Workshop artifact shell with Mishra's Workshop and lock pieces like Sphere of Resistance.
2. A blue shell with Force of Will and Brainstorm, borrowed from the Lurrus decks.
3. The Legacy Sewer Combo shell plus Vintage power (Moxen, Black Lotus, Ancestral Recall, Time Walk, Tinker), using 4 Pyroblast and 1 Red Elemental Blast as the counter suite.

I picked the third. Workshop can't cast your two key creatures, and the deck doesn't have enough blue cards to pay for Force of Will. Pyroblast is strong against a field that is mostly blue.

**Odds and other notes:**
- On the play, you see Welder or Gamble by turn 3 about 57% of the time, and an Extruder, Cam, Engineer or Tinker 86% of the time. Both together is about 48%, before counting Ancestral Recall, Wheel and Moxite drawing you into pieces.
- The checker's 0.1% figure for the turn-3 line counts drawing all five cards, including Skateboard, which you don't need. It also ignores tutors.
- The checker flagged Melded Moxite, Phyrexian Dragon Engine and Red Elemental Blast as rarely played in Vintage. I kept them:
  - Moxite's discard puts Extruder into the graveyard.
  - Dragon Engine is something Welder or Engineer can bring back, and when it enters from the graveyard you can swap your hand for three new cards.
  - Red Elemental Blast is extra hate against the blue decks.
- The deck runs only 16 lands, against about 20 the checker recommends, because it plays 11 mana artifacts. That matches the Vintage Shops decks' land count.
- The 15-card sideboard covers Dredge, Paradoxical Outcome and storm-style combo, Shops, the white Initiative deck and Oath.

--- After playtest ---
I resubmitted the deck and it was accepted.

**1. No payoff or lock piece: fixed.** I cut 2 Melded Moxite and added 1 Karn, the Great Creator and 1 Wurmcoil Engine.
- **Karn** is colorless, so Ancient Tomb and Moxen can cast it. Its static ability stops the opponent from activating their artifacts' abilities, which turns off their Moxen, Sol Ring and Paradoxical Outcome mana. Its −2 gets Ensnaring Bridge, Grafdigger's Cage or Tormod's Crypt from the sideboard.
- **Wurmcoil** is a second big creature for Welder and Tinker to bring out, alongside Chaos Defiler.
- I kept 2 Moxite so the deck still has some ways to discard artifacts into the graveyard.

**2. Mana clash: fixed as suggested.** I cut 2 Ancient Tomb and added Steam Vents and a third Mountain. The deck now has 9 blue sources (up from 2 blue lands) and 16 red sources. Tomb-heavy hands are much rarer.

**3. Low-impact cards and blasts that Misstep answers: mostly fixed.** I added 3 Force of Will. To make room I cut Skateboard and 1 Pyroblast, and only 1 Sewer-veillance Cam instead of the suggested 2.
- **Why keep 3 Cam:** the reviewer called Cam's tap/untap trigger low-impact, but that trigger is the infinite loop. Welder trades Cam for Extruder, Cam leaving untaps Welder, Extruder deals 2 damage, then Welder trades back and Cam's ETB untaps Welder again. Four Goblin Engineer can also put either piece into the graveyard, so 3 Cam is plenty.
- **Force of Will** gives the deck a counter that Mental Misstep can't answer. Cam, Ancestral, Walk, Tinker and Misstep are all blue cards it can exile to cast it for free.
- **Cost of cutting Skateboard:** a Welder can't use the loop the turn it lands any more. The loop now waits a turn, so it realistically finishes on turn 3.

**Draw odds:** the check reports a 0.2% chance of drawing every card in the line by turn 3. That number counts Karn as a required card, even though he's only the backup plan, and it doesn't simulate Engineer's search or the card draw. So the real chance of assembling the combo is higher, but I don't have a number for it.

The final list is 60 cards with 16 lands, and the sideboard is unchanged.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
I built a **Boros metalcraft aggro deck**, labeled as a brew. No published Pauper list in the last 400 days plays Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum together, so this is new territory.

**The three directions I considered**
1. Take the clues, Battle Screech and Kor Skyfisher package from the menu's Mono-White Aggro deck.
2. Build blue/white Affinity around Thoughtcast and Myr Enforcer.
3. Use the shell of the Boros "Synthesizer" deck, which runs Glint Hawk, Kor Skyfisher, white artifact lands (Ancient Den) and Galvanic Blast.

**Why I picked the third:** it's the only one where all three of your cards do real work. Ancient Den and other artifact lands make Recruit's metalcraft work, the 1-mana creatures make Captain cheap, and Drum taps a creature for mana of any color, which fixes red for Bolt and Galvanic Blast and gives Glint Hawk something cheap to bounce and replay.

**The plan**
- **Turn 1:** Ancient Den, Ornithopter (costs 0), then Springleaf Drum. That's three artifacts. Tap the Drum with Ornithopter for white and cast Ardent Recruit, which is already a 3/3.
- **Next turns:** Add Glint Hawk, Kor Skyfisher and Thraben Inspector, all of which add to or reuse your artifacts.
- **Search Party Captain:** It costs 1 less for each creature you attacked with. Attack with three creatures and cast it after combat for just W. It's a 2/2 that draws a card.
- **The finish:** Galvanic Blast deals 4 damage once you have three artifacts. It and Lightning Bolt clear blockers or finish the game around turn 5.

**Things to know**
- **Land count:** 18 lands, while the Synthesizer lists run about 20.5. I went lower on purpose: the average mana value is 1.43, and the 4 Drums act as extra mana sources.
- **Odds:** you have Recruit by turn 2 in about 45% of games. Some artifact (land, Drum, Ornithopter, Inspector and so on) shows up by then about 99% of the time, so Recruit is usually a 3/3 by turn 2 or 3 when you do draw it.
- **The win line is an example, not a combo.** You'll draw every card in that exact sequence by turn 5 almost never (about 0.1%). The deck wins through interchangeable cheap threats plus burn, not one specific chain.
- **Sideboard:** it targets the biggest decks in the meta: Red Elemental Blast for Terror and Faeries, Dust to Dust and Smash to Dust for Affinity, Electrickery for Elves and the white token decks, Prismatic Strands for Madness, and Relic of Progenitus for graveyard decks.

--- After playtest ---
The revised deck was accepted at 60 cards and 19 lands. I changed the mana base and kept all three cards you asked for at 4 copies each.

1. **Captains clogging and too few lands:** I added a 19th land but kept all 4 Search Party Captains, since they're one of your requested cards. To make room I cut Journey to Nowhere from 3 to 2. The extra land should get the Captains cast instead of sitting in hand. Kor Skyfisher bouncing lands still adds flow.
2. **Metalcraft and red mana:** I swapped both Wind-Scarred Crags for Great Furnace #3 and #4, and made the 19th land Rustvale Bridge #4. The deck now runs 12 artifact lands instead of 7, so Galvanic Blast and Ardent Recruit turn on much more often. Red sources went from 9 to 12, and white sources are 13.
3. **Springleaf Drum:** I kept all 4. It's a requested card and the turn-1 Recruit engine. With more artifact lands, a Drum that can't make mana still counts toward metalcraft, so it's no longer a dead card. Swapping it for Lembas would weaken one of your core cards just for the Madness matchup.

**Odds:** The listed win line needs 8 specific cards drawn by turn 5, which happens in only about 0.1% of games. In practice the deck wins with any similar mix of cheap flyers, metalcraft and burn, not that exact sequence.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built **Boros Eidolons**, a new red-white brew (no published list plays these three cards together). It's a low-curve aggro deck that runs 24 multicolored spells. The deck passed the legality check and was accepted.

**The plan:** The two Eidolons are meant to be thrown away. Sandstorm Eidolon ({R}, sacrifice) stops their best blocker from blocking. Aurora Eidolon ({W}, sacrifice) prevents 3 damage, which can save an attacker from a block or a burn spell. Every red-white spell you cast after that returns both from your graveyard to your hand, including:
- the hybrid creatures (Boros Recruit, Battlegate Mimic, Spirit Mascot itself)
- the two-color creatures (Wojek Halberdiers, Skyknight Legionnaire)
- Pursue the Past, which also lets you discard an Eidolon to draw two

Each time an Eidolon comes back, or you flash back Pursue the Past or Battle Screech, cards leave your graveyard and Spirit Mascot gets a +1/+1 counter. The typical game goes Recruit on turn 1, Mascot on turn 2, then Skyknight or Battle Screech. You use the Eidolons to clear blockers each turn and aim to win around turn 6.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Red-white aggro with the Battle Screech package from Mono-White Aggro. I chose this one.** The hybrid creatures count as white, so they pay Screech's flashback cost of tapping three white creatures, and every flashback grows Mascot.
2. Red-white-blue control with Ephemerate and Lórien Revealed. This had too few multicolored spells to bring the Eidolons back reliably.
3. Red-white-green with Verdant Eidolon and Naya Hushblade. The mana base was much worse.

I picked the first because it's the only one where all three cards feed each other on every turn.

**Things to know:**
- **Copies:** The Eidolons are 3 of each rather than 4. They keep coming back, so one copy gets used many times, and six 4-mana 2/2s is already plenty for an aggro deck.
- **Lands:** 18, using the mana setup of the existing Boros Aggro deck. That deck runs about 19 lands, but this one's curve is lower (average mana value 2.33). The hybrid costs also make colour requirements easier.
- **Odds:** The submission tool says you'll have drawn every card in the full sequence by turn 6 in only about 0.5% of games. That number undersells the deck, because the pieces swap in for each other: any of the 24 multicolored spells brings the Eidolons back, and any Eidolon or flashback grows Mascot.
- **Sideboard:** 15 cards aimed at the top decks right now: Madness, Terror, Affinity and Elves.

--- After playtest ---
I resubmitted the revised deck and it was accepted as legal at 60 cards. I took all three suggested fixes, but changed two of them slightly.

**1. Eidolons stuck in hand.** I cut 1 Sandstorm Eidolon and 1 Wojek Halberdiers, not one of each Eidolon, and added 2 Prismatic Strands. Strands saves the team from Bolt and Fiery Temper, its flashback taps a white creature, and casting the flashback grows Spirit Mascot. The Eidolons are the cards you asked for, so I kept 3 Aurora (white, easy to cast, protects the team) and 2 Sandstorm (the harder one to cast). The sideboard drops from 3 Strands to 2 to stay at four copies total, and the open slot goes to a fourth Journey to Nowhere. One correction to the review: the Eidolons are 2/2s, not 3/3s, which is more reason not to hard-cast them.

**2. Slow, white-heavy mana.** I cut Sacred Peaks and 1 Plains for 2 Mountain. That leaves 18 lands with 12 red sources and 11 white, and one fewer tapland. I kept Kor Skyfisher and the Garrisons: returning a Garrison with Skyfisher gets the land's mana back, and Skyfisher is a gold spell that brings back Eidolons.

**3. Thin Spirit Mascot payoff.** I cut 2 Battlegate Mimic for 2 Faithless Looting. Looting turns stuck Eidolons into new cards and puts them in the graveyard for the next gold spell. Its flashback also grows Mascot. Now 6 cards can discard Eidolons (4 Pursue the Past, 2 Looting) instead of 4, and 16 cards can grow Mascot by leaving the graveyard.

**How it wins:** It's still the same plan, finishing around turn 6. The tool says all 8 cards in the win line are drawn by turn 6 in only 0.1% of games. That's because the line lists every piece of the engine, and you don't need all of them at once to win.

**What I didn't fix:** Looting is mono-red, so it doesn't bring Eidolons back by itself. You still need to cast a gold spell afterward to return them.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I built **Living Death Druid**, a Premodern combo brew. Living Death is the finisher, and the creatures it brings back make the opponent lose life when they enter play.

**How it wins:** Get creatures into your graveyard early, then cast Living Death. It sacrifices every creature on both sides and puts every creature card from your graveyard onto the battlefield.
- Each **Laquatus's Champion** that enters makes the opponent lose 6 life.
- Each **Soul Scourge** makes them lose 3 more.
- **Akroma** returns with haste and attacks for 6 in the air, and the opponent has no creatures left to block.

**Getting creatures into the graveyard:**
- **Hermit Druid:** the deck has zero basic lands, so one activation puts your entire library into the graveyard. Only activate it when Living Death is already in your hand. Done that way, it gives you up to 24 life loss from the Champions, 6 from the Scourges and 6 from Akroma.
- **Buried Alive:** puts three Champions in, which is 18 life loss from one Living Death. The opponent is usually left at 2 or less with no creatures, facing three 6/3s.
- **Survival of the Fittest:** discard a creature to find a Champion, then discard that Champion to find the next one.
- **Insidious Dreams:** you discard cards to cast it, so discarding Champions fills the graveyard while it puts Living Death on top of your library.

Dark Ritual, Birds of Paradise, Wall of Roots and Phyrexian Tower get you to 5 mana on turn 3–4. Cabal Therapy and Duress protect the combo from counterspells like Stifle, which matters because the Stifle/Phyrexian Dreadnought deck is 15% of the field.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **The menu's Hermit Druid Combo shell:** its mana, zero basic lands, and its Birds, Wall of Roots, Survival and Cabal Therapy, with Living Death plus Champions as the kill.
2. **A fairer BG Survival deck:** Living Death as a board reset with value creatures.
3. **Mono-black Dark Ritual reanimator** built on Buried Alive.

I chose the first and folded in the best part of the third (Dark Ritual and Buried Alive). It's the only version where Living Death actually ends the game the turn you cast it, and it gives you three separate ways to fill the graveyard.

**Odds:** You have Living Death or Insidious Dreams by turn 4 about 68% of the time, an enabler about 89%, and both together about 60%. The checker's 0.2% figure assumes you draw every card in the win line, but the payoff creatures are meant to reach the graveyard without being drawn, so it doesn't apply.

**Weak points:**
- Living Death is a sorcery, so a counterspell or Stifle on it beats you. Use your discard first.
- Graveyard hate in the opponent's sideboard is a real problem.
- If Hermit Druid mills your library and the opponent somehow survives, you lose when you have to draw from an empty library.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the current top decks: Xantid Swarm and Duress against the blue counterspell decks, Engineered Plague, Smother and Diabolic Edict against the creature decks, and Naturalize, Uktabi Orangutan and Ray of Revelation against Enchantress and the Oath decks.

--- After playtest ---
I fixed all three problems. The resubmitted deck was accepted, still at 60 cards and Premodern-legal.

1. **Hermit Druid could mill my whole library.** I cut 2 Reflecting Pool for 1 Swamp and 1 Forest. Druid now stops at the first basic it reveals and puts it into my hand. Each activation should mill about a third of the library (my estimate), so I can use it every turn without decking myself, instead of leaving it on the board as a chump blocker.
2. **Living Death was too slow and there was no cheap backup.** I cut 2 Insidious Dreams for 2 Animate Dead. It costs 2 (black plus 1) and brings back a Champion (opponent loses 6) or Akroma right after Druid, Buried Alive or Survival. I chose Animate Dead over Exhume because Exhume also lets the opponent return a creature, which could give Stiflenought back a discarded Dreadnought. Real Hermit Druid Combo lists also play Animate Dead more often than Exhume.
3. **Not enough cheap mana.** I cut the main-deck Duress for a 4th Wall of Roots. That makes 12 mana accelerants (4 Birds, 4 Wall, 4 Dark Ritual), so it's easier to keep 1 mana up for Daze when casting Buried Alive. Duress moved to the sideboard, which now has 3 for blue matchups.

To keep the sideboard at 15, I dropped Ray of Revelation for that third Duress.

The win line is the same: fill the graveyard, then cast Living Death. Four Champions (24 life) plus two Soul Scourges (6) is 30 life lost, and Akroma swings for 6 in the air if more damage is needed. The target is still turn 4.

The checker reported 0% for drawing every card in the line by turn 4. That's expected, because the deck never needs all those cards in hand. The point is to get them into the graveyard, mostly through Druid, Buried Alive and Survival, and the checker doesn't simulate those.

problems.problem: Hermit Druid in a deck with zero basic lands mills the entire library. It only works when Living Death is already in hand and 6 mana is available that same turn; otherwise I deck on my next draw. Both Druids sat on the board as chump blockers, and that will be true most games.
problems.fix: Cut 2 Reflecting Pool for 1 Swamp and 1 Forest so Druid becomes a repeatable, safe self-mill engine; or cut the Druids for a 4th Wall of Roots and 3 Animate Dead.

problems.problem: Living Death costs 5, and the deck has few fast ways to reach that mana or to reanimate more cheaply. Against Daze, Stifle and Counterspell decks the payoff comes on turn 6-7, far too slow against a turn-4 12/12. Insidious Dreams (4 mana, card disadvantage) is a weak slot in a deck this mana-hungry.
problems.fix: Cut 2 Insidious Dreams for 2 Exhume (or Animate Dead) as cheaper reanimation that also turns on off Buried Alive and Survival.

problems.problem: Too little cheap acceleration to back up the 3-mana setup spells. Buried Alive tapped out into Daze, and the deck has only 3 Wall of Roots beyond Birds and Dark Ritual. The discard suite is too thin to clear counters before going off.
problems.fix: Cut Duress for a 4th Wall of Roots, and play Buried Alive with 1 mana spare against blue to pay for Daze.
